text_summary.body: In Josiah's days Pharaoh Necoh went up "to"/"against" the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates; Josiah went to meet him and Necoh killed him at Megiddo when he saw him; his servants carried him dead in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him; the people of the land anointed Jehoahaz.

setting.body: ABC 3: in Nabopolassar's 16th year (610/609) the Babylonians and Medes took Harran from Aššur-uballiṭ and "the army of Egypt that had come to help him"; in the 17th year, in Du'ûzu (June/July 609), Aššur-uballiṭ "with a large army from Egypt" crossed the Euphrates and besieged Harran until Ulûlu without success. Necho's march north is this campaign. Josephus says Necho was marching "to fight with the Medes and Babylonians".

constraints.textual_assertion: Jehoahaz … reigned three months in Jerusalem. Pharaoh Necoh put him in bonds at Riblah
assumptions: Josephus: three months and ten days (Ant. 10.5.2).

locations.role: Place of the battle and of Josiah's death (Kings)
Burial; place of death in Chronicles and Josephus

terminology.gloss: The preposition can mean "against", "to" or "on behalf of"; WEB and KJV render "against", NKJV "to the aid of". ABC 3 shows that Egypt fought on Assyria's side.
A collection of laments for Josiah, not the canonical book of Lamentations (Curtis and Madsen; Payne via Guzik).

competing_reconstructions.label: Necho marching to help Assyria against Babylon
competing_reconstructions.summary: Josiah tried to stop an Egyptian army going to Assyria's aid.

competing_reconstructions.label: Necho marching against Assyria (610)
proponents: J. R. Lumby (1887), before ABC 3 was published
competing_reconstructions.summary: Read the Hebrew as "against" and supposed Josiah an ally or tributary of Assyria. Superseded by the chronicle on the direction of the campaign.

competing_reconstructions.label: Herodotus's battle at "Magdolos" against "the Syrians" is this battle
proponents: C. F. Keil (1872): a confusion with Megiddo
F. C. Movers (as reported by Keil): Migdol on the Egyptian frontier
competing_reconstructions.summary: Herodotus 2.159 has Necho defeat the Syrians at Magdolos and then take Cadytis.

competing_reconstructions.label: Necho came by sea (landing at Acco) vs by land
proponents: C. F. Keil (1872) and J. R. Lumby (1887): by sea
E. L. Curtis and A. A. Madsen (1910): Megiddo was simply the old battle-ground; against Cheyne's sea route
competing_reconstructions.summary: Keil infers a landing at Acco from Herodotus's mention of Necho's fleet; Curtis rejects the inference.

competing_reconstructions.label: Who warned Josiah: Necho (Chronicles) or Jeremiah (1 Esdras)
proponents: 2 Chr 35:21–22 (text): words of Neco "from the mouth of God"
1 Esd 1:28: "the words of the prophet Jeremy from the Lord's mouth"
competing_reconstructions.summary: The Greek parallel transfers the warning to Jeremiah; Curtis and Madsen regard the message as probably a literary construction.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik follows 2 Chr 35:20–25: Josiah ignored Necho's warning, disguised himself and was shot by archers; Clarke places the mourning at Hadad-rimmon (Zech 12:11).

open_questions: Why Josiah opposed Necho (Keil: to keep Judah from Egyptian control; Lumby: loyalty to Assyria) is not stated in the text.
The Megiddo excavations' Iron Age strata were not researched.
